record.original_question: Study the first non-integrable point-vortex systems on non-orientable surfaces, and describe the corresponding Casimirs and finite-dimensional approximations for area-preserving diffeomorphism groups of those surfaces.

evidence.quote: Problem 29. Study the first non-integrable cases for a small number of point vortices on non- orientable surfaces. Describe the full set of Casimirs and finite-dimensional approximations for the group of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of non-orientable surfaces, analogous to the ones in the orientable cases.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a closed non-orientable smooth surface (e.g. the real projective plane $\mathbb{RP}^2$ or the Klein bottle) endowed with an area form $\mu$ (defined locally up to sign, i.e. a density). The group $\mathrm{SDiff}(N,\mu)$ of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of $N$ acts on its Lie algebra of divergence-free vector fields, and dually on the space of vorticity functions (more precisely, pseudo-functions / twisted densities adapted to non-orientability). A system of $n$ point vortices on $N$ with strengths $\Gamma_1,\dots,\Gamma_n\in\mathbb{R}$ is the Hamiltonian dynamical system on (a desingularization of) $N^n$ obtained by lifting to the orientable double cover $\widetilde N \to N$ and using the Green's function of the Laplacian on $\widetilde N$ together with the deck involution, producing equations of motion for the positions $x_1,\dots,x_n\in N$ governed by a Hamiltonian of Kirchhoff–Routh type.

Solve the following:

(a) Determine the smallest number $n$ of point vortices for which the system on $N$ fails to be Liouville-integrable, and exhibit explicit non-integrable examples for $N=\mathbb{RP}^2$ and $N=$ Klein bottle, together with proofs of non-integrability (e.g. via Melnikov, symbolic dynamics, or topological entropy arguments).

(b) Describe the full set of Casimir invariants for the natural Lie–Poisson structure on the dual of the Lie algebra of $\mathrm{SDiff}(N,\mu)$ for a closed non-orientable surface $N$, in analogy with the generalized enstrophies and circulations known in the orientable case.

(c) Construct finite-dimensional Lie-algebra approximations of $\mathrm{SDiff}(N,\mu)$ for non-orientable $N$ (analogous to the $\mathfrak{su}(n)$-type approximations of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of the sphere and torus), and prove a suitable convergence statement.
artifact.category_tag: Point vortices and area-preserving diffeomorphism groups
artifact.status_search_result: Parts of the problem have been addressed: a Hamiltonian formulation of point vortices on non-orientable surfaces (including the Klein bottle and RP^2) has been developed via the orientable double cover, and recent work classifies generic coadjoint orbits and Casimirs (generalized enstrophies plus circulations) for area-preserving diffeomorphisms of closed non-orientable surfaces. However, an explicit identification of the smallest non-integrable point-vortex configurations on non-orientable surfaces, and explicit finite-dimensional approximations of the corresponding diffeomorphism groups analogous to the su(n) approximations in the orientable case, do not appear to be fully established.

status_evidence.title: Coadjoint orbits of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of non-orientable surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of generic coadjoint orbits for the group of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of a closed non-orientable surface, completing Arnold's program.
status_evidence.claim: Coadjoint orbits and Casimirs for area-preserving diffeomorphisms of non-orientable surfaces have been classified.

status_evidence.title: A Hamiltonian approach for point vortices on non-orientable surfaces II: the Klein bottle
status_evidence.snippet: Hamiltonian approach to point vortex motion on non-orientable surfaces via the orientable double cover.
status_evidence.claim: A Hamiltonian formulation of point vortices on the Klein bottle has been established.

status_evidence.title: Classification of Casimirs in 2D hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Complete list of Casimirs for 2D Euler hydrodynamics on surfaces without boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Casimirs (generalized enstrophies and circulations) classified for orientable surfaces, with extensions to non-orientable cases.
